To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of economic growth and FDI on carbon emission is heterogeneous across quantile.
the relationship between economic growth, foreign direct investments and carbon emissions is heterogeneous.

FDI is positively correlated with carbon emissions in BRICS countries and negatively correlated with carbon emissions for G7 countries, and the relationship between economic growth and carbon emissions is inverted U shaped in G7 countries but U shaped in BRICS countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of economic factors on carbon emissions in G7 countries, and the impact of economic and foreign investment factors on carbon emissions, in BRICS countries.
the relationship between economic growth and carbon emissions in G7 countries, BRICS countries, and all countries.

the effect of economic development and foreign direct investment (FDI) on carbon emissions, and it provides new evidence on the relationship between economic growth and carbon emissions in both G7 and BRICs countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FDI is not always beneficial for carbon emissions reduction.
the impact of foreign direct investment on the environment is ambiguous, which is consistent with the existing literature.
the impact of the independent variables (economic growth and FDI) on carbon emissions is not the same across quantiles and countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FDI can be a useful policy tool in controlling environmental degradation.

FDI has a significant impact on carbon emissions in G7 countries, while it is insignificant in BRICS countries; the relationship between economic growth and carbon emissions is inverted U shaped in G7 countries but is U shaped in BRICS countries, and the effect of economic growth and carbon emission is heterogeneous across quantile.
the environmental protection policy should be different in the G7 countries and BRICS countries, and the policy makers need to consider the heterogeneity in the environmental policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EKC hypothesis holds for G7 countries, and that the pollution haven hypothesis holds for BRICS countries.
the effect of FDI on CO2 emissions is heterogeneous across different quantiles.
the EKC hypothesis should be taken into consideration when formulating environmental policy.
